Normalise read depth against a reference

Source: R/normalise.R
normalise_depth.Rd

Expected counts per bin and cell, and the log2 ratio of observed to expected (centred per cell). Every reference of a cell leaves that cell out.

  • loo: the pseudobulk of all other reference cells.

  • celltype: the pseudobulk of the other reference cells of the same cell type; cells without a type, and types with fewer than min_cells_type reference cells, use loo. The normal-tissue reference: it removes the cell-type-specific chromatin signal in the depth.

  • model: a robust Poisson GLM of the bin counts on GC content, mappability proxies and peak coverage, plus a per-cell GC trend. The tumour reference: it needs no copy-number-normal cells.

Usage

normalise_depth(
  scn,
  method = "loo",
  use = NULL,
  cell_type = NULL,
  ref_cells = NULL,
  min_cells_type = 20,
  per_cell_gc = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

scn

scn object

method

"loo", "celltype" or "model"

use

logical bin filter (default bin_filter() on bins and counts)

cell_type

cell type per cell (default scn$cells$cell_type)

ref_cells

optional selector of cells allowed as references (e.g. clean singlets)

min_cells_type

celltype: types with fewer reference cells fall back to the global reference

per_cell_gc

model: subtract a per-cell robust GC trend after the shared GLM

...

unused

Value

scn_norm: list(method, ratio (bins x cells log2, NA on unused bins), expected (bins x cells counts, NA on unused bins), use, size, params)
